Cause-Based Plan Jaipur

Dark Circles Treatment in Jaipur | Treating the Cause

Dark circles are shadows or discolouration under the eyes. They can come from extra pigment, thin skin that lets the blood vessels show through, hollows that cast shadows, or puffiness, and many people have more than one of these. At Kezza, our skin doctors work out the cause first and then plan treatment at our Jaipur clinic.

Understanding Dark Circles

What Causes Dark Circles?

The skin under the eyes is among the thinnest on the body, so small changes show easily. Cleveland Clinic lists ageing, family history, extra pigment from sun exposure, poor sleep, dehydration, eye rubbing and hollow tear troughs among the causes, along with stress, alcohol and smoking. Dark circles are also more common in people with darker skin tones.

In brown skin, the most common reason is extra pigment (periorbital hyperpigmentation), which gives a brown or greyish colour that may run in families and worsen with sun, rubbing or allergies. When the skin is thin, the purple-blue colour of the veins beneath can show through. With age, the fat pad under the eye thins and a groove forms, which casts a shadow even if the skin colour is normal.

Because each of these causes needs a different treatment, the most important step is a proper examination. A cream that lightens pigment will not fill a hollow, and a filler will not lighten pigment.

In Short:

  • Pigment: brown or grey colour in the skin itself.
  • Hollows: a groove that casts a shadow.
  • Right treatment: depends on which cause you have.
Types

Types of Dark Circles

Pigmented

Brown or grey-brown colour that does not change much when the skin is gently stretched. Common in Indian skin.

Vascular

A blue or purple tint from visible blood vessels under thin skin, often worse when you are tired.

Structural

A hollow or tear-trough groove that casts a shadow, which looks darker under overhead light.

Puffy

Swelling or bags under the eyes that create a shadow below them, sometimes linked to allergies or fluid retention.

Mixed

Most people have a combination, so plans often combine more than one treatment.

Lifestyle-Related

Poor sleep, eye rubbing, dehydration and screen strain can make any type look worse.

Suitability

When to Seek Treatment for Dark Circles

Dark circles are usually harmless. Treatment is about how they look and how you feel, once other causes are ruled out.

Treatment may help if

  • Dark circles make you look tired even when you are rested
  • Concealer and good sleep have not made enough difference
  • You have pigmentation, hollows or both under your eyes
  • You are ready to protect the area from the sun and follow a home routine

See a doctor first if

  • The darkness or swelling appeared suddenly, affects only one eye, or comes with pain or vision changes
  • You have itching, eczema or allergies around the eyes, which need treating first
  • You are pregnant or breastfeeding, when some treatments are avoided
  • You have had fillers or eyelid surgery before, or bruise easily

If lines around the eyes bother you as well, anti-wrinkle injections for crow's feet can be discussed at the same consultation.

Your Plan

How Dark Circles Are Treated at Kezza

Your plan follows the cause, starting with the simplest steps.

01

Examination

Your doctor looks at the area in good light, gently stretches the skin and checks for hollows, puffiness, allergy and eye rubbing.

02

Home Routine

Daily sunscreen, a gentle eye cream chosen for the cause, and advice on sleep, allergies and rubbing.

03

Pigment Treatment

For pigmented circles, prescription creams, mild chemical peels or laser toning, spaced a few weeks apart.

04

Hollow Treatment

For tear-trough hollows, a hyaluronic acid filler may be suggested, given by an experienced doctor.

05

Review

Progress is reviewed with photos, and the plan is adjusted to your response.

Timeline

Dark Circles Treatment Timeline

Pigment fades slowly, while filler changes show sooner.

W2

Two Weeks

The full effect of a tear-trough filler is usually visible at about two weeks.

W4

Four Weeks

Peel or laser sessions are repeated every few weeks for pigment.

M2

M6

Medical Note: Results vary from person to person. This page is general information from Kezza Hair & Skin Clinic and is not a substitute for a consultation with a doctor.

Treating pigmented dark circles

Pigment under the eyes builds up slowly, so it fades slowly too. Daily broad-spectrum sunscreen, including on cloudy days and indoors near windows, is the foundation, along with not rubbing the eyes. Your doctor may prescribe a cream to lighten pigment and repair the skin barrier. Mild chemical peels designed for the delicate eye area and laser toning can speed up the change over a course of sessions. In brown skin, stronger treatments are avoided because irritation can trigger more pigment.

Treating hollows and tear troughs

When the shadow comes from a groove rather than colour, adding a small amount of hyaluronic acid filler along the tear trough can smooth the transition from lower eyelid to cheek, so less shadow forms. Cleveland Clinic notes that not everyone is a good candidate, because some people become puffy after fillers in this area, and that the effect lasts about one to two years. The area has many small blood vessels, so tear-trough filler should only be given by an experienced doctor who can manage complications.

Home care that helps

  • Use sunscreen and sunglasses every day.
  • Avoid rubbing your eyes, and treat allergies or eczema that make you rub.
  • Aim for regular sleep, and try sleeping with your head slightly raised if you wake up puffy.
  • A cold compress for a few minutes can reduce morning puffiness.
  • Concealer with a peach or orange tone can hide brown-grey circles on Indian skin while treatment works.

Setting realistic expectations

Most people see a clear improvement rather than a complete change. Pigment tends to improve over months and needs maintenance, fillers change the shadow sooner but need top-ups, and inherited dark circles may always be slightly visible. Your doctor will explain what is likely for your type before you start.

What affects the cost of dark circles treatment?

The cost depends on the cause and the treatments needed. A home routine with prescription creams costs less than a course of peels or laser sessions, and filler is priced by the amount used. Your doctor explains the plan and the total after examining you.

FAQs

Frequently Asked Questions

Can dark circles be removed permanently?
There is no single cure, because dark circles have several causes and some, such as family history and ageing, cannot be changed. Treatment can make them clearly lighter or less shadowed, and a home routine with sun protection helps keep the improvement.
Do under-eye creams work?
Creams with ingredients chosen by your doctor can slowly lighten pigment and support thin skin, but they cannot fill a hollow or remove bags. Results take weeks to months, and sunscreen matters as much as the cream.
Are under-eye fillers safe?
In experienced hands, hyaluronic acid fillers are widely used for tear-trough hollows, but they are not for everyone. Redness, swelling and bruising are common for a few days, and lumps, a bluish tint under the skin or long-lasting puffiness can occur. Rarely, filler blocks a blood vessel, which can damage the skin or, very rarely, cause permanent loss of sight, so it should only be given by an experienced doctor who can dissolve it straight away.
Does laser treatment work for dark circles?
Laser toning can help pigmented dark circles over several sessions. It does not treat hollows. In brown skin, settings must be chosen carefully, because heat can sometimes cause more pigment, which is why the plan is gradual.
Will more sleep get rid of my dark circles?
Good sleep helps when tiredness is part of the cause, because poor sleep can make the skin look paler and shadows deeper. It will not change pigment or hollows, which is why many people still see dark circles after resting well.
How long do results last?
It depends on the treatment. Lightened pigment can return with sun exposure and rubbing, so maintenance matters. Cleveland Clinic notes that under-eye fillers usually need a top-up every one to two years.
